trust_decision.summary: The page tag is untrusted data that reaches SQL text in three page-delete sites and must be escaped at each query construction with DbService::escape() (mysqli_real_escape_string); the defect is that three sinks interpolate the tag raw while the rest of the same code family already escapes it.

landing_point.why: The advisory summary names ApiController::deletePage, and that method's DELETE into the links table is the first thing an engineer who read only the summary opens.

fix_sites.entry_point: DELETE /api/pages/{tag} (and POST /api/pages/{tag}/delete, which delegates to the same method)
<PageTag>/deletepage handler with eraselink=oui&confirme=oui (before-callback of the deletepage handler)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The tags-tool file is only a before-callback of the UI deletepage handler that repeats the core delete logic with the legacy $this->Query()/$this->config['table_prefix'] API in another package, so a solver will argue the advisory's ApiController::deletePage is the real site and the tool handler is a legacy duplicate.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: The same $tag is handed to PageManager::getOne(), UserIsOwner(), isOrphaned() and PageController::delete(), which each escape it internally, and the links DELETE is deliberately skipped for orphaned pages; escaping the tag earlier in the method (or dropping the isOrphaned guard) double-escapes it, so the page is no longer found/deleted and the API returns 500 instead of 200.

O6_input_shapes: single quote inside the page tag read back from the stored pages row (second-order, $page['tag'])
single quote inside the tag as sent verbatim in the API path before the page lookup
backslash / double quote / NUL in the tag (covered because the fix uses a full mysqli_real_escape_string, not a quote-doubling shortcut)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: The despam spam-cleanup restore action builds "update <prefix>pages set latest = 'N' where latest = 'Y' and tag = '" . $revision['tag'] with an unescaped page tag read back from the pages row (same second-order tag-into-SQL property, different statement from the delete sink).
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: It is an admin-only spam-cleanup action (whole action gated by UserIsAdmin at tools/security/actions/despam.php:23) that updates a revision during restore rather than deleting page links, so it can be argued out of the advisory's delete-API scope.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: separate package (tools/security/actions) reached from the despam page action, one file away from the landing controller

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Bulk admin page delete over an array of posted tags hitting the identical DELETE FROM links WHERE to_tag sink.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: A maintainer already wrote this parallel admin CRUD route with the same getOne/isOrphaned/delete sequence, so an unescaped copy of it (or a new bulk action on the same table) is a natural sibling; it already escapes, which shows the pattern is copy-and-paste prone.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second tag-driven delete route in the tags tool that calls PageController::delete() without any links cleanup.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The tags tool already duplicates delete behaviour in a jsonp handler; adding the inbound-links DELETE there (as the two fixed files do) would reproduce the sink, and the tag would be a GetPageTag() value.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Bulk delete of an array of posted comment tags (suppr[]) through PageController::delete().
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: This action already mass-deletes pages from a request array; extending it to clear inbound links per tag is exactly how the fixed sites came about, and the array input shape differs from the single-tag API route.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Tag-table cleanup in the delete path (deleteAll) delegating to TripleStore::delete for each stored tag value.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: It is called from PageManager::deleteOrphaned during every page delete, so any change to how the tag is passed to TripleStore would put the same unescaped-tag mistake one layer deeper, in internal machinery the check never calls.

O9_family: SQL injection (CWE-89), second-order: a stored page tag re-used raw in a DELETE/UPDATE

O10_build.toolchain: PHP 8.3 with ext-mysqli, ext-gd, ext-curl, ext-zip, ext-mbstring; composer 2 (composer.json build scripts, composer install also builds tools/autoupdate); PHPUnit 12 via tests/tests.sh
services: PHP web server / front controller index.php for the HTTP API
O10_build.project_tests: PHPUnit suites under tests/ and tools/*/tests run by tests/tests.sh; they cover acls, groups, users, performers and archive, but none covers page deletion or the links table, so the fix adds no regression test (the diff touches only three source files).

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Wrap only the ApiController::deletePage DELETE value in escape()/addslashes(), or escape $tag once at the top of the method, leaving the two handlers untouched and breaking the later getOne/delete calls by double-escaping.

out_of_scope_notes: Not pursued: tools/tags/actions/admintag.php:11 puts $_GET['delete_tag'] (a comma list) inside 'id IN (...)' using mysqli_real_escape_string rather than intval - an id-list shape, not this advisory's page-tag property.
Not pursued: tools/tags/services/TagsManager.php:92 ignores its $page argument and uses GetPageTag() - an unrelated functional bug.
Not pursued: actions/EraseSpamedCommentsAction.php:84-93 and tools/security/actions/despam.php:137-145 delete pages without removing their inbound links rows - a cleanup gap, not an injection.
unverified: Repo size in MB could not be measured without shell access (repo_mb left null).

Whether the two handler sites are reachable with a quote-bearing tag at all: the query-string tag grammar (includes/constants.php:31,40) allows only [\p{L}\-_.0-9] and is enforced in includes/YesWikiInit.php:97-113, so those two sites look like defensive fixes; I found no second path that sets GetPageTag() from stored page data (includes/YesWiki.php:246-253 only copies the row matched by the validated URL tag).

Exact ACL semantics of the '+' route option (ApiService::isAuthorized) were not read; the reachability argument relies on includes/YesWikiInit.php:219 default_write_acl '*' plus an authenticated user.
No latest release/code was supplied (inputs: none), so present_in_latest for the O8 route is unknown and no latest/path:line could be cited.
Recall risk could not be checked against any write-up (no network); rated low from the advisory being a single-repo GHSA/CVE with no known public analysis.
